title: Transport of colimit cocones across an equivalence of diagrams
statement:
Use quasicategories, small simplicial sets, coherent diagrams, coherent transformations, equivalence edges, mapping spaces and cocones in the universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory, let $K$ be a small simplicial set, and let $F,G:K\to\mathcal C$ be coherent diagrams. Let $\tau:F\to G$ be an equivalence edge of $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$. For every vertex $x\in\mathcal C$, precomposition with $\tau$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_D(G,\Delta_Kx)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_D(F,\Delta_Kx).$$
For any coherent cocone $\lambda:G\to\Delta_Kx$, choose a composite $\lambda\tau:F\to\Delta_Kx$ with its composition triangle in $D$. Then $\lambda\tau$ is colimiting if and only if $\lambda$ is colimiting. This assertion requires neither diagram to admit a previously chosen colimit and also holds for the empty simplicial set $K$.

source.place: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Lemma 4.2.4.3 (printed p. 257) and Section 4.2.1; agent-extracted equivalence-transport consequence of the cocone mapping-space criterion. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$. Since $\tau:F\to G$ is an equivalence edge, choose an inverse edge $\rho:G\to F$ and 2-simplex witnesses for $\rho\tau\simeq\mathrm{id}_F$ and $\tau\rho\simeq\mathrm{id}_G$. The chosen composition triangle for $\lambda\tau$ is precisely a representative of the composite in $D$ needed below.

source.place: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Section 4.2.1: equivalence edges and coherent composition; Lemma 4.2.4.3

proof.text: For every vertex $x\in\mathcal C$, the simplicial set $D$ is a quasicategory and its mapping spaces are Kan complexes by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Let $p_{\tau,x}:\operatorname{Map}_D(G,\Delta_Kx)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(F,\Delta_Kx)$ and $p_{\rho,x}:\operatorname{Map}_D(F,\Delta_Kx)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(G,\Delta_Kx)$ be precomposition by $\tau$ and $\rho$, i.e. the restrictions of the canonical composition class of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] to the vertices $\tau$ and $\rho$. Restricting the associativity homotopy for the objects $G,F,G,\Delta_Kx$ to the vertices $\tau,\rho$ gives $p_{\rho,x}p_{\tau,x}\simeq$ precomposition by a composite of $\tau$ and $\rho$ in $M(G,G)$. The 2-simplex witness for $\tau\rho\simeq\mathrm{id}_G$ gives that composite the component class of the degenerate identity edge, precomposition depends only on the component class, and unitality makes precomposition by the identity homotopic to the identity map; so $p_{\rho,x}p_{\tau,x}\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Symmetrically, with the objects $F,G,F,\Delta_Kx$ and the witness for $\rho\tau\simeq\mathrm{id}_F$, $p_{\tau,x}p_{\rho,x}\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Hence both precomposition maps are homotopy equivalences, in particular equivalences of spaces.

source.place: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Section 4.2.1 and Lemma 4.2.4.3: mapping-space composition with an equivalence edge

proof.text: Fix $x$ and a coherent cocone $\lambda:G\to\Delta_Kx$. For any vertex $y\in\mathcal C$, the dual cocone criterion says that $\lambda$ is colimiting exactly when the map $q_{G,y}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(G,\Delta_Ky)$, $a\mapsto(\Delta_Ka)\lambda$, is an equivalence for every $y$; that is, $q_{G,y}$ is $\Delta_K$ on mapping spaces followed by precomposition $p_{\lambda,y}$ with $\lambda$. For the composite cocone, $q_{F,y}=p_{\lambda\tau,y}\circ\Delta_K$. The chosen composition triangle has edges $\tau,\lambda,\lambda\tau$, so $[\lambda\tau]=[\lambda][\tau]$ in $hD$; since precomposition depends only on the component class, $p_{\lambda\tau,y}$ is homotopic to precomposition by the canonical composite of $\lambda$ and $\tau$, which by the associativity homotopy (objects $F,G,\Delta_Kx,\Delta_Ky$, restricted to the vertices $\tau,\lambda$) is homotopic to $p_{\tau,y}p_{\lambda,y}$. Hence $q_{F,y}\simeq p_{\tau,y}q_{G,y}$ for each $y$ separately; no coherence in $y$ is needed.

source.place: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Section 4.2.1 and Lemma 4.2.4.3: cocone mapping-space criterion

proof.text: By Step 2, $p_{\tau,y}$ is an equivalence for every $y$. Therefore $q_{F,y}$ is an equivalence for every $y$ if and only if $q_{G,y}$ is, by Step 3 and two-out-of-three for equivalences of spaces. Applying the cocone criterion gives that $\lambda\tau$ is colimiting if and only if $\lambda$ is colimiting. The criterion and all constructions allow arbitrary small $K$, including the empty simplicial set, and no colimit object was assumed to exist in advance.

source.place: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Lemma 4.2.4.3 and Section 4.2.1: equivalence-transport conclusion

proof_origin.place: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Lemma 4.2.4.3 and Section 4.2.1; expanded mapping-space proof of equivalence transport for cocones
